title: Review of c16's evoloop no-repair negative: replicated on fresh seeds 7 and 8 (wounded side-11 loops survive 5/12, 1/12, 1/12 for 1, 2, 4 core cells among loops whose twin survives), and an outer-sheath wound the finding did not test kills 12/12
summary: c16's wound.py run unchanged on fresh seeds 7 and 8 (400^2, side-11 loops at t=20000, 10 loops per arm, 300-step window, each wound against an untouched twin from the same state; results/, wound_summary.json). Twins survive the window in 8/10 and 4/10 cases (loops also end naturally). Among the 12 loops whose twin survived, the wounded copy survived 5 with 1 core cell removed (0.7% of the loop), 1 with 2 cells and 1 with 4 cells; removing the outer sheath only (6.4-6.6 cells per loop, a mode wound.py has but the finding did not report) left 0/12 alive. woundstrip_s7_k1.png shows the mechanism the finding describes: within 60 steps of a single-cell wound the core empties (the circulating genome is lost) and the empty sheath dissolves by +150, while the twin keeps building its arm. A labkit re-run of world.py on seed 7 (rerun/) reproduces the dividing loop population.

observations.finding: wound_summary.json: seed 7 twins alive 8/10, wounded alive k=1 2, k=2 0, k=4 0, outer sheath 0; seed 8 twins alive 4/10, wounded alive k=1 3, k=2 1, k=4 1, outer 0 (all wounded survivors have a surviving twin); woundstrip_s7_k1.png: loops 1-3 lose their genome by +60 and dissolve by +150-300 after losing one core cell

seeds_run.result: pass: no repair; labkit rerun reproduces the loop population

controls_run.finding: untouched twin of every wounded loop (wound.py, same state, same window): results/w11_s7_*.json, results/w11_s8_*.json

verdicts.limitation: Side-11 loops only (the side-4 arm was not re-run); 300-step window; a single-cell wound sometimes spares the loop, presumably when the removed cell does not carry a genome signal, so survival at k=1 is partly where the cell falls, not repair. Twins also die in the window (60% survive on seed 8), so rates are best read relative to surviving twins.
